situation:
You are the marketing manager for BRIARFIELD LEARNING, an app-based tutoring service owned by the third generation of the family that opened the original tutoring center sixty years ago. The owner (judge) moved the business onto the app four years ago, and every session is booked through it now.

Roughly half of BRIARFIELD's sessions are in-home visits, where a tutor drives to the student. The company's liability insurer will renew the policy next month only if that changes: it will not cover in-home sessions while the tutors are independent contractors rather than employees of the company. The renewal date is fixed and the insurer has offered no third arrangement.

Making the in-home tutors employees puts them on payroll and under the company's coverage, but the payroll cost raises the hourly session price. That increase falls hardest on the scholarship families who use in-home sessions most, and it works against the promise the founding generation made that no family is turned away over price.

Ending in-home sessions and moving every student to video on the app satisfies the insurer and keeps the price flat for families. It also ends the higher-paying in-home work the tutors count on, and it cuts off the rural families whose home internet will not carry a video session at all.

The owner (judge) wants your analysis of what each course of action does to the business environment BRIARFIELD sells into, to the data the company keeps on why families choose it, and to the clientele three generations have built, together with a recommendation. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of BRIARFIELD LEARNING. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are the third generation of your family in this business and you moved it onto the app four years ago. You want to hear whether the marketing manager recommends making the in-home tutors employees or ending in-home sessions and moving every student to video, and you want to hear how anyone would know later on whether the decision was the right one.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us we had made a mistake?
